system_note: Reviewed entire MR_12 record (History & Physical (Admitting); Trauma Surgery consult; CT trauma panscan; Critical Care progress notes; Medication Administration Record; Discharge/Transfer Summary) and the relevant condition policies. Principal diagnosis S36.032A (major splenic laceration) is supported: CT documented a Grade IV splenic laceration with active extravasation and the record documents an emergent splenectomy during the same encounter (History & Physical; CT Trauma Panscan). The splenic injury thereby meets the policy validation criteria for S36.032A (AAST Grade III-V and operative splenectomy) (Policy Documents/DRG/Splenic Injury.docx). Femoral shaft fracture S72.301A is supported by CT (displaced mid-shaft right femur fracture) and operative management (intramedullary fixation) documented in notes and the problem list. Traumatic shock T79.4XXA is supported by explicit provider attribution to hemorrhagic/traumatic shock, objective hemodynamic data (SBP 78 on arrival, lactate 5.4), MTP activation and operative hemorrhage control (History & Physical; Medication Administration Record; Critical Care Progress Note) and meets the policy criteria for traumatic shock. However, three coding errors were identified that drive this Finding: (1) Pelvic ring code severity is miscoded: the claim lists S32.810A (stable pelvic ring, CC) but the record documents unstable/open-book pelvic ring injury (Tile B1) with symphyseal diastasis 3.5 cm, bilateral posterior SI disruption, active pelvic hemorrhage requiring IR embolization and external fixation - the treating team documents the pelvis as "unstable" and performed external fixation (CT Trauma Panscan; History & Physical; problem list). Per the pelvic policy, that documentation supports S32.811A (unstable pelvic ring, MCC) rather than S32.810A. (2) R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is billed but there is no documentation of cardiogenic/pump-failure physiology or an explicit provider attribution to cardiogenic shock; clinical documentation consistently attributes shock to hemorrhage/trauma and documents MTP, transfusion, and surgical/IR hemorrhage control (History & Physical; Critical Care Progress Note; Medication Administration Record; Policy Documents/DRG/Traumatic Shock.docx). Remove R57.01. (3) S06.340A (traumatic hemorrhage of cerebrum) is billed but the CT trauma panscan explicitly states "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage; mild scalp hematoma," and the problem list records a mild traumatic brain injury (GCS change) without intracranial bleed - the intracranial hemorrhage code is unsupported and should be removed. All other billed diagnoses/procedures (including splenectomy 07TP0ZZ, IM nail 0QQ606Z, pelvic external fixation 0SH90BZ, IR occlusion 04L33DZ, chest tube 0WH30YZ, endotracheal 0BH17EZ, transfusion 30233N1, central line 02HV33Z, and prolonged ventilation 5A1D90Z) are supported by the operative/ICU notes, imaging, MAR, and the discharge summary. Citations: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp. 604-249; Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Trauma Panscan, Chart Notes, p. 588; Trauma Surgery Consultation, Chart Notes, pp. 652-588; Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, pp. 249-652; Medication Administration Record, PHARMACY, pp. 402-152; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 869-870; Policy Documents/DRG/Splenic Injury.docx (Validation Criteria); Policy Documents/DRG/Pelvic Ring Disruption.docx (Validation Criteria); Policy Documents/DRG/Traumatic Shock.docx (Validation Criteria). Based on the above, the corrected complete diagnosis list and procedure list are provided below.
rationale_letter: Re: DRG Audit Determination - MR_12 Dear Provider, We reviewed the inpatient record for patient Beauregard L. Thibodeaux (admit 05/07/2026) for the above-referenced trauma admission and the codes billed on the claim. After a three-way review of the medical record against applicable coding policy, we have identified a Finding that affects DRG assignment. The principal splenic injury and most procedures are supported, but several diagnosis-level corrections are required. Finding: The claim currently lists S32.810A (multiple fractures of pelvis with stable disruption - CC), R57.01 (cardiogenic shock - MCC), and S06.340A (traumatic hemorrhage of cerebrum - MCC). The medical record does not support those billed items as coded. Basis for the Finding (record + policy): - Pelvic severity misclassification: CT trauma panscan documents "Pelvis: symphyseal diastasis 3.5 cm; bilateral posterior sacroiliac joint disruption; active extravasation from right internal iliac branch," and the trauma/orthopedic documentation describes an "open-book pelvic ring injury (Tile B1)" with external fixation performed. The treating team documents the pelvis as unstable (physical exam: "Pelvis: unstable to lateral compression; pelvic binder applied"). Per the pelvic-ring policy, instability (surgeon-documented) with diastasis and operative external fixation/embolization meets the criteria for S32.811A (unstable pelvic ring, MCC). The billed S32.810A (stable ring, CC) therefore understates severity and is incorrect. (See CT Trauma Panscan and History & Physical documentation cited.) - Unsupported cardiogenic shock (R57.01): The clinical documentation consistently attributes hemodynamic failure to traumatic hemorrhage and documents MTP activation, transfusions, operative splenectomy, and IR embolization for pelvic hemorrhage. There is no provider documentation of pump-failure physiology or a diagnosis of cardiogenic shock in the chart; traumatic/hemorrhagic shock is documented and meets traumatic shock policy criteria (T79.4XXA). R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is not supported and should be removed. - Unsupported intracerebral hemorrhage (S06.340A): The CT trauma panscan explicitly documents "Head: no acute intracranial hemorrhage; mild scalp hematoma," and the problem list records a mild traumatic brain injury without intracranial bleed. S06.340A is therefore unsupported and should be removed. Supported items (no change): S36.032A (major splenic laceration, AAST Grade IV - supported by CT and operative splenectomy), S72.301A (right femoral shaft fracture with IM nailing), traumatic shock T79.4XXA, J95.851 (MSSA VAP), N17.9 (AKI), D62 (posthemorrhagic anemia), I82.401 (right lower-extremity DVT), Z90.81 (acquired absence of spleen/status post splenectomy) and the listed procedures (splenectomy, IR embolization / occlusion, external fixation, IM nailing, chest tube, endotracheal intubation, transfusion, central line, and prolonged ventilation >96 hours) are supported by the operative notes, imaging and medication/ICU records. Correction being made: We will remove R57.01 and S06.340A from the claim and will reclassify the pelvic ring code from S32.810A to S32.811A to reflect documented instability (MCC). The complete corrected diagnosis and procedure lists are attached below. Please see the enclosed citations from the medical record and the applicable coding policy supporting these changes. Corrected diagnosis list (principal first): 1. S36.032A 2. S72.301A 3. S32.811A (replaces S32.810A) 4. S22.42XA 5. S27.4XXA 6. S36.115A 7. T79.4XXA 8. M62.88 9. N17.9 10. J95.851 11. B95.62 12. I82.401 13. F43.10 14. D62 15. Z87.891 16. Z90.81 Corrected procedure list (complete): 0BH17EZ, 07TP0ZZ, 0WH30YZ, 04L33DZ, 0SH90BZ, 0QH60BZ, 0QQ606Z, 30233N1, 02HV33Z, 5A1D90Z If you disagree with this determination, you may submit additional clinical documentation or clinical rationale to demonstrate support for the billed codes as originally submitted (for example, explicit surgeon documentation justifying S32.810A rather than S32.811A, or documented cardiogenic shock physiology attributable to pump failure). Absent additional documentation, we will process the claim with the corrected diagnosis set shown above. Sincerely, Clinical DRG Auditor (References and record excerpts supporting this determination are provided in the enclosed audit evidence.)

evidence_cited.excerpt: CT trauma panscan demonstrated Grade IV splenic laceration, Grade II liver laceration, pelvic ring injury with active extravasation, right femur fracture, and right hemopneumothorax with rib fractures. Emergency intubation was performed for airway protection. Massive transfusion protocol was activated, and the patient was transferred to the operating room for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy, followed by IR embolization for pelvic bleeding.

Distinguish from: Unstable pelvic ring disruption (S32.811A) carries MCC status and reflects rotational or vertical instability requiring emergent hemorrhage control and definitive stabilization. The distinction between stable (S32.810A - CC) and unstable (S32.811A - MCC) is made by the treating orthopedic or trauma surgeon based on CT findings and classification; auditors must not infer stability from radiographic report alone - explicit surgeon documentation of stability/instability is required.
